units.title: Anatomy of a Joint & OA vs RA Joints
units.guide: The knee joint has distal femur, synovium, articular cartilage on the articular surface of bone, joint capsule, synovial fluid and proximal tibia; damage to that cartilage makes every movement hurt. OA loves DIP, PIP and the 1st CMC (spares wrist & MCP), while RA loves MCP, wrist and PIP (spares DIP).

units.title: Osteoarthritis: m/c Joint Disease
units.guide: Osteoarthritis is the most common joint disease, born of age related degeneration or preexisting destruction of cartilage.

units.title: OA: Primary vs Secondary
units.guide: Primary idiopathic OA rules the single-joint knee (also spine, hand) and the generalized DIP. Secondary OA rides on preexisting pathology: intra articular trauma, developmental anomaly, AVN and overweight.

units.title: OA: Pathogenesis Chain
units.guide: Cartilage degenerates, raw bone rubs on bone (pain + sclerosis), poor blood supply makes necrotic cysts, regenerating bone throws off osteophytes — and when those break loose, loose bodies roam freely in the joint.

units.title: OA: Clinical Features
units.guide: OA hurts on active and passive movement, stiffens the joint, crepitates and deforms. Disuse withers the muscle — most often the vastus medialis. Bouchard's (PIP) and Heberden's (DIP) nodes mark the knuckles.

units.title: OA: X-ray Features
units.guide: On X-ray: decreased joint space, bone-on-bone appearance, subchondral sclerosis, necrotic cysts & osteophytes and loose bodies. The medial side carries the load, so the space narrows medially first, bowing the leg into varus — OA is the m/c cause of bilateral genu varum.

units.title: Loose Bodies in the Knee
units.sec: Loose bodies in Knee joint · p192
units.guide: Loose bodies in the knee: osteoarthritis is the m/c cause overall and in the elderly; osteochondritis dissecans wins in the young; and synovial chondromatosis makes multiple bodies.

units.title: OA: Conservative & Medication
units.guide: Conservative care: lose weight to stop progression, physiotherapy with heat and strengthening exercises, walk with support and brace. Medications: NSAID acetaminophen, cartilage protectors (glucosamine, chondroitin sulphate) early on, and hyaluronic acid injections for lubrication.

units.title: OA: Surgical (Definitive)
units.guide: Go definitive with arthroscopy (joint wash to remove loose bodies), high tibial/medial opening wedge osteotomy to correct varus deformity and pain, or arthroplasty to replace the damaged joint — unicondylar for the medial side, or TKR with femoral and tibial components (watch for patellar clunk syndrome).

units.title: THR & RA: Introduction
units.guide: THR replaces the head & neck of the femur plus the acetabular component. Then RA enters: the m/c inflammatory arthritis, a disease of synovium — systemic autoimmune, multisystem (lungs, heart, liver), erosive, females > males, symmetrical peripheral joints: MCP > wrist, PIP in the hand, knee and hip; axial rare (cervical spine); DIP spared. SLE is the only non-erosive inflammatory arthritis.

units.title: RA: Pathogenesis
units.guide: An antigen/antibody reaction ignites synovial inflammation and destruction, erosion marches from periphery to centre, pannus forms and devours the joint, and the sequence ends in subluxation.

units.title: RA: Multisystem & Markers
units.guide: RA shortens life expectancy and travels to the heart (carditis), pleura (pleuritis), lungs (Caplan) and blood (Felty). Diagnose with ↑ ESR/CRP, RF — the most sensitive marker, an IgM against the Fc portion of IgG — and Anti-CCP, the most specific.

units.title: RA: X-ray vs OA
units.guide: RA X-ray: narrowed joint space, osteoporosis & hyperemia (juxta articular first, then generalized), marginal erosions, and no sclerosis, no osteophytes. Opposite of OA, which scleroses. De Quervain's synovitis targets the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis.

units.title: RA: Deformities
units.guide: The RA hand deviates ulnarly at the fingers while the metacarpals deviate radially; boutonniere is PIP flexion with DIP extension, swan neck the reverse; mallet finger affects only the injured digit. The knee bows into bilateral genu valgum (children: rickets > RA; elderly: RA), wind swept and triple deformity. The foot shows hammer toes and hallux valgus; ulnar nerve palsy makes the claw hand.

units.title: RA: Management
units.guide: Preserve function with physiotherapy; methotrexate is the DOC. DMARDs: leflunomide (immunosuppressant), infliximab/Adalimumab (TNF-α inhibitors), anakinra (IL-1 receptor antagonist), rituximab (anti-CD20). Surgery: synovectomy for inflamed synovium, joint replacement and deformity corrections.

units.title: Spondyloarthropathies: Overview
units.guide: Four inflammatory spondyloarthropathies hit the spine and joints: ankylosing spondylitis (m/c), psoriatic, enteropathic (Crohn's/ulcerative colitis) and reactive (Shigella, chlamydia). All are seronegative (RA is RF positive), hit young males, run HLA B27 positive and accompany uveitis.

units.title: AS: Features & Pathogenesis
units.guide: AS — Marie Strumpell/Bechterew's disease — is male-predominant, axial > peripheral, centred on the sacroiliac joint (also spine, hip). Gluteal/back pain with morning stiffness that improves with activity, ↓ lumbar movement, ↓ chest expansion (ribs fuse to spine) and anterior uveitis. Enthesitis at the ligament-tendon insertions erodes, regenerates abnormally and calcifies, restricting motion; first X-ray sign is sacroiliitis with sclerosis and ankylosis.

units.title: AS: Bamboo Spine & Signs
units.guide: The bamboo spine fuses and squares the vertebrae with calcification between them: ligament inflammation builds syndesmophytes, curvature is lost, and bridging syndesmophytes lock the spine. The dagger sign calcifies the interspinous ligament; the trolley track sign calcifies paraspinal and interspinous ligaments.

units.title: AS: Criteria, Tests & Treatment
units.guide: Essential criterion: sacroiliitis — MRI is the IOC (earliest changes, iliac side > sacral side); supporting criteria add ↓ lumbar movement, ↓ chest expansion and inflammatory back pain with morning stiffness. Test with chest expansion measurement, Gaenslen's, FABER/figure-of-4 and pump handle for SI, and Schober for the lumbar spine (distance fails to increase on flexion). Treat with chest physiotherapy, swimming/cycling, NSAIDs and steroids.

units.title: Spinal Fusion: DISH & OPLL
units.guide: When the spine fuses, think beyond AS: DISH (Forestier disease, elderly) flows candle-wax ossification down the anterior longitudinal ligament, while OPLL ossifies the posterior longitudinal ligament, m/c cervical, also in the elderly.

units.title: Psoriatic Arthritis
units.guide: Psoriatic arthritis is erosive, females > males, asymmetrical oligoarticular, m/c at the DIP. CASPAR: psoriasis, RF -ve, X-ray changes, dactylitis (sausage digits), nail changes. Destructive ends: arthritis mutilans (total bone destruction) and the pencil-in-cup phalanx, with digits shortening and telescoping out.

units.title: PsA Treatment & Hemophilia Basics
units.guide: Treat the psoriasis and give methotrexate. Hemophilia: A = factor 8 deficiency, B = factor 9 deficiency; recurrent bleeding destroys the synovium with inflammation. Pseudo tumors are muscle hematomas (iliopsoas > quadriceps) and painful joint swelling bleeds into the joint, m/c the knee.

units.title: Hemophilic Arthropathy: X-ray & Treatment
units.guide: The hemophilic knee rests flexed — its position of ease — and can end in arthritis mutilans. X-ray: widened intracondylar notch, lost joint space, juxta articular osteopenia, squared patella. Treat the bleed: factor replacement, compression bandage, ice pack; aspirate only for severe pain (infection risk).

units.title: Gout: Features & Pathogenesis
units.guide: Gout, the m/c crystal arthropathy, is a purine abnormality with raised uric acid (normal 3.5-6.5 mg/dl), striking the 1st MTP of middle-aged men; furosemide and aspirin precipitate attacks. A sudden uric acid swing drops crystals in cold peripheral joints, ignites local inflammation and damages the joint — tophi mark the acute attack.

units.title: Gout: Investigations
units.guide: X-ray: punched out lesion, joint destruction, overhanging bone (martel sign). The best investigation is synovial fluid analysis under light microscopy: needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals.

units.title: Gout: Treatment
units.guide: Acute attack: only NSAIDs (indomethacin; aspirin is C/I) — colchicine brings GI disturbances. Never chase uric acid levels during an acute attack; it can precipitate more pain.

units.title: Chronic Gout & Pseudogout
units.guide: Chronic gout: xanthine oxidase inhibitors (allopurinol, febuxostat, rasburicase) and the uricosuric probenecid. Pseudogout deposits calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate — elderly, females > males, a/w hypothyroidism, m/c the knee; X-ray shows chondrocalcinosis (also in ochronosis/alkaptonuria, hemochromatosis, hyperparathyroidism) and the fluid holds polygonal, positively birefringent crystals.

units.title: Neuropathic (Charcot) Joint
units.guide: The Charcot joint destroys itself silently — lost sensation and proprioception, m/c from diabetic peripheral neuropathy, favouring mid tarsal then tarso metatarsal joints (leprosy, syphilis-knee also). Look for a bag of bones, without pain. Fuse it with arthrodesis; arthroplasty is C/I.
